children.name: Scheduler
children.descr: The scheduler of the program: the tasks and the feed of notes under every one of them - the same lists the owner and the staff see in their windows. Add-only, the way the program keeps it: a task is never edited nor deleted, it moves by a note carrying a state, and kClose ends it. A private task is seen by its author, its executor and the person with id 1. state_key and kind_key are values of TASK_STATE_KEY and TASK_KIND_KEY in the base settings, and the people go by id - the Users tool answers them.

children.name: Currencies
children.descr: The currencies the prices of the store are written in. multiplex is the rate against the base currency - the one whose rate is 1 - and division says a sum is divided by that rate instead of multiplied. A goods points at a currency by its *_curr_id columns and the Price tool writes them; the sums already written into orders keep their own words and never follow a currency.

children.name: Providers
children.descr: The providers of the goods, the groups they stand in and the options hung on them. The option tree - provider_key with the values of provider_key_value - belongs to the program and is only read here; the providers, their groups and the rows of provider_key_set are what this tool writes. A goods points at its provider by store.provider_id, the Price tool writes it, and a currency of one provider points back by currency.provider_id.

children.name: Discounts
children.descr: The discount groups of the store and the rules standing in them. A goods carries a group by store.disc_group_id - the Price tool writes it - and the rules of that group say what the discount is: from_sum is where a rule starts, disc_proc is how much it takes off, and the two days are the ones it lives between. A group holding no rule gives nothing away. A rule writes its currency in sum_curr_id, and the Currencies tool answers those.

children.name: Taxes
children.descr: The taxes of the store. A group holds the rates, and a goods points at a group by its tax_group_id - the Price tool writes that column, not this one. The areas are a tree of their own - a country, a region inside it - and a rule is what ties a rate to an area; a rule may carry a value of its own instead of the one its rate names. The options declared for the areas live in the registry of the additional options, place tax_area, and only the rows set on the areas are written here.

children.name: Orders
children.descr: The orders of the shop. An order is never changed in place: every change is a new version of it, and the version the order stands at now is the one the shop shows. CmdQuery finds and reads orders whole. The work on one order walks in a circle: CmdLoad answers its version as one array - or CmdCreate answers a blank one - the array is shaped in your hands or by the goods and option commands, CmdCalc counts the money the way the shop counts it, and CmdEdit saves the array as the new version of the order. Every step of the circle passes through the very logic the storefront checkout runs - the discounts, the option sums, the refusals of the shop included - and never straight into the tables. The right to see an order goes by the values of its options, a status among them; saving takes the ORDER_VERSION_ADD operation of the store.

children.name: Brands
children.descr: The brands of the goods and the options hung on them. The option tree - brand_key with the values of brand_key_value - belongs to the program and is only read here; the brand rows and the rows of brand_key_set are what this tool writes. A goods wears a brand by its brand_id column, and the Price tool writes it.

children.name: Browser
children.descr: The catalogue as the Browser window shows it, read and never written: the goods of a section or of a whole branch, and the search by any column the sign names. A goods comes with the twenty-one columns that window loads - what it is called, what it costs, its codes, its clan, its days - and with the sections it hangs in. Everything else about a goods belongs to the other tools of the Goods branch: the prices and the stock to Price, the texts to Description, the place in a section to Place. The right is for_browse, given out in the program on the sections a goods hangs in.

children.name: Price
children.descr: The commercial half of a goods: what it costs and how many there are - the prices with their currencies, the supplier, the discount group, the tax group, the stock and the counts on the warehouses, the auto-count, and the parameters standing on it. The right is for_price, given out in the program on the sections a goods hangs in, so only goods hanging in a section of yours are reached here. The other half - the names and the texts a buyer reads - belongs to the Description tool.

children.name: Description
children.descr: The content half of a goods: what a buyer reads about it - the names, the codes, the texts, the seo, the clan and the characteristics standing on it. The very fields the Description window of the program writes back, the price among them, though the money proper belongs to the Price tool. The right is for_frame, given out in the program on the sections a goods hangs in, so only goods hanging in a section of yours are reached here.

children.name: Place
children.descr: Where a goods hangs in the catalogue and in what order it stands there - the rows of topic_store and nothing else. The right is the place one, given out on the section: the section takes the goods in, so whoever owns the section decides. A goods hanging in no section is in the store and in no catalogue at all, and only the Lost tool reaches it.

children.name: Lost
children.descr: The goods that hang in no section: a goods loses its last section and drops out of every window that walks the catalogue - this is where it is found again. From here it goes back into a section, or out of the store for good. Deleting a goods happens nowhere else, and it goes by the operations of a person, not by the right of a section: a goods hanging nowhere has no section to hold a right.

children.name: Goods
children.descr: The loader of the goods: everything a card is made of in one call. Four streams tied by ref, a temporary key of your own - the goods, their characteristics, their parameters, and the sections they hang in. Keys are not weighed here: brands, providers, currencies and the tree of the characteristics are read beforehand and come as ids; only a value of a characteristic may come as a word, and it is looked up under its info_id. The pictures are a call of their own: the store lays a file down before a module runs, and a goods not born yet has nothing to hang it on - take the ids of this answer to the Files tool.

children.name: Files
children.descr: The loader of the files: a pack of them onto the elements in one call, and a derived picture painted beside those that ask for one. It is the second half of an import and goes after the goods: a file hangs on an element by its id, and the ids are what the answer of the Goods loader gave back - write them into the rows of this call. The files themselves ride with the call, so the size of one pack is the size of one request: split a big load into several calls.

children.name: Catalog
children.descr: The sections of the main catalogue: the tree itself, the rights on it, the options hung on it and the alternative catalogues built over it. Every row of an answer says what this person may do on that very section, so read the list before promising anything. The goods themselves are not touched here - only the places they hang in, and the Place tool moves them.

children.name: Attributes
children.descr: What a buyer reads about a goods: the tree of the characteristics with its folders, and the values every one of them takes. The tree comes whole, the values are asked for by their characteristic - a live shop keeps thousands of them. The rights are a pair - the characteristic itself and its values - and they are given out on the characteristic, in the program.

children.name: Parameters
children.descr: The parameters of the goods: the commercial properties the prices are built of - warranty, delivery, a margin of its own - and the values each one takes, every value with the sum it carries and the currency of that sum. Not what a buyer reads about the goods: that is the characteristics, and the Attributes tool keeps them.

children.name: Promo blocks
children.descr: The promo blocks of the shop: a tree of blocks, and under every one of them the texts it shows, the goods it gathers, the places it hangs in and the option rows set on it. The types - kind_key here, obj_key on a link - are values of ADVERT_KIND_KEY, ADVERT_TEXT_KIND_KEY, ADVERT_GOODS_KIND_KEY, ADVERT_LINK_KIND_KEY and ADVERT_LINK_OBJ_KEY in the base settings, and the Settings tool answers them. The pictures of a text belong to the Files tool, element advert_text.

children.name: Settings
children.descr: The settings the people of the shop change themselves - the window of the program calls them Settings. What a setting is and where it stands is declared by the developer in the registry, and the User settings tool keeps that; here only the value moves. A person changes a setting when the branch it stands on was given to them or to their group, and CmdList says of every setting whether this person may.

children.name: File
children.descr: The files of the elements - the photographs of the goods above all. One tool for every element, because one table shape serves them all: a file is a row of files_<entity> and a picture on the disk. The group of a file (kind_key) is what a template picks it by, and the group words are values of the FILES_<ENTITY> codes in the base settings. The right is that of the element the file hangs on. No tool deletes a picture from the disk: rows go, and the idle-files audit of the owner reclaims the space.

children.name: Profile
children.descr: The picture profiles: the recipes a derived picture is made by. A profile holds one of two kinds of size: width and height - an exact size, or resolution - megapixels spread over the shape of each picture. A picture is sized in this order: size_base takes the area as it is and reads no size of the profile; else width and height; else resolution in the shape of the area; over 50 megapixels nothing is painted; size_optim keeps an area smaller than the size on both sides; smart lets the canvas take the shape of the area, else the rest of the canvas is background - the picture itself is never stretched; border makes the picture smaller by two margins along its long side. A profile is a row of the FILES_PROFILE dictionary, but its body is XML of the program's editor, so it is read and written here, in plain words. The area is the whole picture here - a frame is cut by hand in the program only; everything else a profile keeps. A mask is a value of FILES_MASK in the base settings with a picture hung on it by the Files tool - entity key_value, elem_id the id of that value.

children.name: Settings
children.descr: The registry of the settings of this shop: the base lists the whole program picks from, and the settings the people of the shop change themselves.

children.name: Basic settings
children.descr: The base settings of the shop: the tree of the codes and the values every code keeps - the lists the whole program picks from, from the kind of a goods to the style of a section. The tree of the codes belongs to the platform and is only read; the values are what this tool writes. A value marked sys_key is one the platform relies on by its very name: its text may be changed, but not that name, and it cannot be removed.

children.name: User settings
children.descr: The settings the people of the shop change themselves: the groups in a tree, and in every group the settings with the mask their text is typed by, plus the rights that say who sees a group. What the storefront reads out of them is the business of the modules.

children.name: Additional options
children.descr: The registry of the additional options: what may be hung on the rows of an entity - sections, attributes, brands, suppliers and their warehouses, parameters and their values, people, groups of people, promo blocks, filters and tax areas. Every call names its place, and the answer is the tree of the options declared there with the values every one of them keeps. Setting an option on a row of an entity is not done here: the tool of that family writes its own *_key_set and takes key_id and value_id from this one. An option is addressed by its skey, in a module as in the program, so two of one name in one place are refused.

children.name: Custom filters
children.descr: The filters an operator picks in the window that asks the server for data: a filter is a query of the developer answering the ids of its place - the goods, the orders or the customers. A parameter written as :NAME in that query is asked for when the filter is used; :NAME@ALIAS is picked from a value list instead of typed, and those lists are the second table here - their own queries run against the local base of the program and answer ID and NAME.

children.name: Users
children.descr: The people of the shop, the groups they stand in and the rights they hold - a right is an operation of the oper tree, handed to a person or to a group. A password is never a field of a call: it is born in the tool, kept as md5 and said once. What a person did in the shop keeps their id, so one who carries history is blocked rather than deleted.
